The story unfolds in "real-time," where the story time (a brief, two-minute encounter outside a café) closely matches the real-world time it takes to read it. Rather than awkwardly compressing their shared history into long expository paragraphs or over-stretching the moment with heavy internal monologues, the writer uses brief stage directions—such as a bus passing, a hesitation to take a cup, or a beat of silence—to naturally pace the dialogue. Meanwhile, years of past relationship history and time spent apart are effectively compressed into the subtext of their short,clipped exchanges (e.g., references to how things were "früher" [before] and whether he still takes sugar). This balance creates an authentic, tense, and emotionally resonant rhythm.
